title: Hr Assistant
company: Clockwork Organisation Ltd t/a Travail Employment - Agency - Contract
description:
HR Assistant
Up to 15 per hour
Monday to Friday
37 hours per week
9-Month Fixed Term Contract
Wrexham

We are currently recruiting for an experienced HR Assistant to join a busy and supportive team based in Wrexham. This is an excellent opportunity for a HR professional looking for an immediate start, providing comprehensive administrative support across the employee lifecycle, recruitment, payroll, and HR processes.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage the end-to-end recruitment and onboarding process, including DBS and Right to Work checks.
- Support employee lifecycle activities including flexible working requests, sickness absence management, annual leave calculations, and other HR processes.
- Provide administrative support for payroll and recruitment activities.
- Maintain accurate employee records, ensuring all information is updated within HR and payroll systems.
- Respond to employee and manager queries via email, telephone, and face-to-face communication.
- Arrange meetings and coordinate facilities as required.
- Maintain records, manage documentation, and circulate agendas where necessary.
- Process purchase orders and BACS payment requests, ensuring finance systems are updated accurately.
- Handle routine and ad-hoc enquiries, escalating matters where appropriate.
- Ensure confidentiality is maintained and all activities comply with GDPR and relevant policies.
- Provide support and cover for other members of the team when required.

The Ideal Candidate
- Previous HR Administration or HR Assistant experience is essential.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding, and employee lifecycle processes.
- Knowledge of payroll administration would be advantageous.
- Strong understanding of GDPR and handling confidential information.
- Excellent organisational skills with strong attention to detail.
- Confident communicator with the ability to build effective working relationships.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office and HR systems.
- Able to prioritise workload and manage multiple tasks effectively.
- Proactive, flexible, and willing to support the wider team.
- Available to start ASAP.

To Apply
Travail Employment Group is operating as an Employment Agency.
To apply for this position, please call Emma on (phone number removed) for more information.

Alternatively, once you click to apply your application will be received immediately by Travail Employment Group. If your application is successful, a consultant will contact you within 7 days. If we have not contacted you within 7 days, you may not have been successful on this occasion, but please feel free to call us to discuss similar roles.
All candidates registering with Travail Employment Group will need to provide proof of identity and evidence of any experience, training and qualifications required for this position.

title: Office Coordinator
description:
Recruit 4staff are representing a well-established environmental services business in their search for a Office Coordinator to work in Wrexham

Job Details:
- Pay: £26,483 - £27,500 per annum
- Hours of Work: Once trained, will move onto a 4-week rotating shift pattern. Week 1: 6:00am - 2:30pm. Weeks 2, 3 & 4: 8:30am - 5:00pm
- Duration: Permanent
- Benefits: Standard pension, free parking, 20 days holiday plus bank holidays (increases with length of service)

Job Role: The Office Coordinator will provide administrative support within a busy recycling depot, supporting Operations Managers with day-to-day activities, completing proactive and reactive route planning for drivers, producing reports and assisting with operational administration. This Office Coordinator opportunity offers full training and the chance to develop valuable logistics and transport planning skills within an established environmental services business.

- Previous administration experience
- Strong organisational and communication skills
- Desire to learn and develop new skills
- Ability to work accurately in a fast-paced environment
- Good attention to detail
- Ability to succeed as an Office Coordinator within a busy operational environment

Advantageous Skills, Experience, or Qualifications
- Previous route planning experience
- Experience within transport, logistics, recycling or environmental services sectors
- Knowledge of driver scheduling and planning processes

Additional Information
- Based within a busy recycling depot
- Full training provided
- Free parking available
- Permanent Office Coordinator opportunity with long-term prospects

Commutable From: Wrexham, Chester, Flint, Denbighshire

title: Unison Branch Administrator
description:
Adecco are pleased to be recruiting for a Unison Branch Administrator to work within the North Wales Police Force

Our client, a prominent organisation in the public services sector, is seeking a dedicated Unison Branch Administrator to join their team in Colwyn Bay. This part-time 18.5 hours per week Monday to Friday role offers an hourly rate of 14.10 per hour and is set to run until March, 2027. The successful candidate will play a key role in providing essential administrative support to the North Wales Police UNISON Branch.

Key Responsibilities:

As a Unison Branch Administrator, the responsibilities will include:
- Performing general administrative duties such as word processing, formatting documents, and managing diaries.
- Responding to inquiries from both internal and external sources with professionalism and efficiency.
- Organising, scheduling, and attending events, meetings, and conferences for the North Wales Police and UNISON.
- Preparing agendas and taking minutes to ensure smooth communication within the organisation.
- Making travel arrangements for branch officers and representatives, utilising the Atriis system.
- Managing and distributing UNISON information leaflets and merchandise.
- Maintaining accurate records and ensuring confidentiality in accordance with policies and procedures.

Requirements:

Our client is looking for candidates who can demonstrate:
- An NVQ Level 3 in Administration or equivalent experience.
- Intermediate IT skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and a typing speed of at least 35wpm.
- Strong communication skills, essential for effective interaction with various stakeholders.
- Previous experience in providing administrative support, including meeting preparation and minute-taking.
- A proactive attitude, with the ability to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.
- Teamwork capabilities, as well as the ability to work independently using one's initiative.

Why Consider This Role?

An opportunity to contribute to a vital organisation dedicated to public service.
A supportive work environment that values professionalism and efficiency.
The chance to develop and enhance administrative skills within a dynamic team.

If you are a motivated individual with a passion for administrative support and a commitment to delivering high-quality service, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply now and take the next step in their career with our client. This is a fantastic chance to make a meaningful impact in a supportive environment!

Apply Today!

Adecco is a disability-confident employer. It is important to us that we run an inclusive and accessible recruitment process to support candidates of all backgrounds and all abilities to apply. Adecco is committed to building a supportive environment for you to explore the next steps in your career. If you require reasonable adjustments at any stage, please let us know and we will be happy to support you.

Adecco acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and an employment business for the supply of temporary workers. The Adecco Group UK & Ireland is an Equal Opportunities Employer.

title: IT Projects Administrator
description:
Job Title: Projects Administrator

Location: St Asaph - Onsite

Salary: 26,000 - 28,000 per annum

Job Type: Full-time, Permanent

Ready to take the first step in your project career? We're looking for a driven, highly organised and enthusiastic Projects administrator to join our growing team, with plenty of opportunity to learn, develop and progress in one of the UK's fastest-growing MSPs.

About Flotek:

Flotek Group is the UK's fastest-growing Managed Service Providers, delivering IT, Cyber Security, Communications and Managed Print solutions to small and medium-sized businesses. With regional sales and support hubs across the UK, our ambitious growth story is built on a simple foundation: every product and service we deliver is backed by expertise, passion and heart. We're a values-led business, and our people are at the centre of everything we do.

About The Role:

We're looking for a highly accurate individual with a keen eye for detail who enjoys a fast pace of work. You will play a key role in supporting our Engineers ensuring the smooth delivery of installations from start to finish. Excellent communication is essential as you'll need to communicate with internal and external stakeholders. You'll also be responsible for coordinating stock and documentation as well as managing engineers' diaries to schedule installations.

Day-to-day activities include:
- Raising and managing purchase orders, ensuring stock is tracked and allocated to the correct projects
- Answering incoming calls to the Projects queue
- Managing all incoming and outgoing stock
- Coordinating engineer documentation - permits, job packs and completion photos
- Scheduling engineers' diaries and allocating resources across projects
- Working closely with the Billing and Finance team to meet strict invoicing deadlines and ensure all financial documentation is accurate and submitted on time
- Scheduling deliveries and site access for Engineering
- Providing day-to-day administrative support to the Projects Team Managers

Skills / Experience:
- Microsoft office including Excel - knowledge of analysing data and Excel functions
- Previous use of CRM/PSA software
- Experience in a similar role within the data cabling, IT or telecoms industry (preferred)
- Stock management

Benefits:
- Opportunities for professional growth and development.
- Staff Share Equity Scheme - your piece of the "Purple Pie"
- 21 Days Holiday increasing to 25 with 4 years of service (+ bank holidays)
- Your birthday off

Due to the nature of the role the company will not be able to offer sponsorship or relocation assistance so candidates must already reside in the UK.

Please click the APPLY button to submit your CV for this role.

Candidates with the experience or relevant job titles of; IT Project Operations Administrator, MSP Projects & Logistics Administrator, IT Project Coordinator, MSP Project Coordinator may also be considered for this role.

title: Operations & Fulfilment Coordinator (Part Time)
description:
Job Description Operations Coordinator

Role at a glance

Hours:- 24 Hours per week, three full days, or spread across Monday to Friday by agreement

Location:- Flint, Mainly on site, with scope for some hybrid working once established

Salary:- £15.25 p/h

Contract:- Permanent, Part Time

About us

We are a small team where everyone's work matters and good ideas are acted on quickly.

The role

This is a hands-on role that combines purchasing, order administration and warehouse work. You will make sure customer orders are bought in, checked, packed and dispatched correctly and on time.

Over time you will take ownership of the day-to-day operational work currently handled by the Director, so that problems are picked up and solved without needing to be escalated.

For the successful candidate there will be growth opportunities.

Key responsibilities

Purchasing
- Raise purchase orders from the sales orders and check them for accuracy.
- Send purchase orders to our manufacturers with the required due dates.
- Check order confirmations against the dates and prices. Chase corrections where needed and update the system.
- Keep prices on purchase orders accurate and up to date.

Sales orders and dispatch
- Liaise with customers on product specifications and order details, working with the Directors where needed.
- Adjust and finalise sales orders so they are correct and ready to invoice before dispatch.

Warehouse
- Handle goods in and goods out.
- Carry out quality checks, pack orders for dispatch.

Technical support
- Help with pre-wiring of equipment. Training will be given.
- Cover warehouse and technical tasks during colleagues' holidays.

Continuous improvement
- Follow our established processes accurately.
- Look for better ways of working and suggest improvements. Good ideas will become part of how we work.

About you

Essential
- At least 2 years' experience in a similar role, such as purchasing, order processing, operations or warehouse coordination.
- A proven track record of solving problems and getting things right first time.
- Experience improving or correcting working procedures.
- A practical, hands-on approach, and happy to move between desk work and the warehouse.
- Sound judgement and the confidence to make sensible decisions without constant supervision.
- Strong attention to detail, especially with dates, prices and order information.
- Confident using computers, order or stock systems, and email.
- Open to trying new ways of working, and able to challenge existing methods constructively.

Desirable
- Experience with Unleashed or a similar ERP system.
- Knowledge of electrical or engineering sector.
- Forklift licence, or willing to train.

What we offer
- £15.25 per hour for 24 hours per week.
- Flexible hours pattern: three full days, or shorter days across the week.
- Scope for some hybrid working once you are established.
- Training in our products, systems and processes, including pre-wiring.
- A varied role in a small team where your ideas shape how the business runs.
- Workplace pension.

title: Relief Ward Clerk
description: The ability to speak Welsh is essential for this post An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Relief Ward Clerk to join the Team at Glan Clwyd Hospital. To work as a member of a team providing an efficient and comprehensive clerical support service for the Ward thereby supporting the delivery of high quality service to patients and staff within the Department. This is a great opportunity to work in and part of the NHS and support your communities with their Health Care. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for patients, relatives and visitors to the Ward and must demonstrate a professional and sensitive manner and maintain confidentiality at all times. Working as part of the Ward Team the post holder will be required to give efficient clerical support to the nursing staff on the Ward. Applicants must also have a good standard of education, be adaptable and have good organisational skills. A professional telephone manner is essential to receive and respond courteously to all telephone enquiries regarding patient care.Previous Ward Clerk experience and knowledge of the Patient Administration System (WPAS) is desirable but not essential as full training will be provided. You will be able to find a full Job description and Person Specification attached within the supporting documents or please click Apply now to view in Trac.
